paper_metadata.title: Efficient option pricing with unary-based photonic computing chip and generative adversarial learning

summary: The paper demonstrates a photonic-chip implementation of unary European option pricing with iterative amplitude estimation on a 3-asset/3-bin proof-of-principle device, using 6 waveguide inputs and up to m=50 amplification steps. It also reports an on-chip GAN distribution-loading module trained for 100 iterations on 8 bins, reaching an L2 norm that stabilizes around -18 dB, but without a demonstrated practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Photonic-chip implementation of unary European option pricing with distribution loading, payoff calculation, and iterative amplitude estimation for a 3-asset / 3-bin proof-of-principle case.

algorithm.variant: Iterative amplitude estimation without phase estimation in a unary photonic circuit
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Repeated amplitude amplification steps up to m=50; accuracy assessed by convergence of payoff standard deviation and error

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Asset-price distribution is binned into unary basis states; each bin is represented by a pair of waveguides (2n-dimensional Hilbert space for n bins) with an ancilla encoded by the second waveguide in each pair
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate European option expected payoff C(ST,K)=∫_K^∞(ST-K)dST via ancilla measurement probability after payoff rotation and amplitude estimation
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection / measurement of ancilla waveguides encoding |1⟩; unary mapping avoids non-local controlled gates

problem_instance.description: European option pricing for three asset values / three bins on a fabricated photonic chip

dataset_specification.description: Log-normal and normal target distributions used for GAN training; option-pricing proof-of-principle uses three asset values

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Continuous price distribution mapped into n discrete bins; payoff angles normalized by maximum asset price smax; strike K used to define in-the-money bins
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Experimental comparison of theoretical payoff vs measured payoff; standard deviation over 50 measurements per amplitude-estimation step; convergence tracked as m increases from 0 to 50

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: Post-selection strategy mentioned for unary scheme; no formal mitigation protocol reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Binning of Monte Carlo paths into unary basis; GAN used to learn/load asset distribution
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Ancilla measurement probability converted to expected payoff; raw angles shifted back to original angles for comparison

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Payoff standard deviation converges from ~0.2 to <0.004 as amplitude-estimation iterations increase

speedup_claims.conditions: for option-pricing sampling error / number of calls to D and P operators
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states quadratic speedup in the number of calls to the distribution-loading and payoff operators; experimental figures show improved convergence but not a full asymptotic benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/√m) in sampling error / O(1/√N) style quadratic improvement over classical Monte Carlo; paper states quadratic speedup in number of calls to D and P
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/m) for Monte Carlo convergence as stated in paper

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; proof-of-principle only for 3 asset values / 3 bins
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Photonic chip with 6 waveguide inputs; iterative amplitude estimation up to m=50; 50 measurements per step
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup only, which Hoefler-style constant-factor analysis makes unlikely to be practically advantageous
No large-scale benchmark against a strong classical implementation on the same problem size
Distribution loading and photonic hardware overhead are not quantified

notes: num_qubits not explicitly stated; inferred as not directly reported because the photonic implementation is described in terms of waveguides/path encoding rather than a qubit register. Hardware is a real photonic chip.

The paper claims quadratic speedup in amplitude estimation and shows convergence of payoff standard deviation from about 0.2 to below 0.004 as m increases to 50, but this is a small proof-of-principle experiment rather than a demonstrated practical advantage.

experiments.description: On-chip generative adversarial network (GAN) training to learn and load log-normal and normal asset-price distributions into the photonic unary option-pricing circuit.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid GAN with photonic generator and classical discriminator; Wasserstein GAN training
algorithm.optimizer: Gradient-free evolutionary algorithm for generator; gradient descent for classical discriminator
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Training complete when generator output matches target distribution; convergence assessed over 100 iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Probability distribution encoded in waveguide occupation probabilities of a unary photonic state; 8-bin chip used for GAN demonstration
problem_formulation.objective_function: Learn a generator distribution matching a target market distribution via adversarial training

problem_instance.description: Distribution-learning task for asset-price distributions used to upload market data into the option-pricing chip

dataset_specification.description: Target distributions are log-normal and normal; real samples drawn from desired probability distributions

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Fake samples are photon occupation probabilities across waveguide modes; real samples are target distribution samples
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare generator output distribution to target distribution; track ℓ2 norm over 100 training iterations; final stabilization around -18 dB

hardware.framework: TensorFlow for discriminator; photonic chip control not otherwise specified

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: Wasserstein distance used to stabilize GAN training; no hardware noise model reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Real samples drawn from target distributions; generator parameters set by phase shifters on chip
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Discriminator scores used to update generator; ℓ2 norm computed between fake and real distributions

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: ℓ2 norm decreases and stabilizes around -18 dB

speedup_claims.caveats: GAN is presented as a distribution-loading method for the photonic option-pricing pipeline; no asymptotic or empirical speedup over a classical baseline is quantified for the GAN itself.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Hybrid photonic generator plus classical discriminator; 8-bin demonstration; 100 training iterations; final L2 norm stabilizes around -18 dB
limiting_factors: No classical baseline comparison for the GAN training task
No asymptotic speedup is claimed for the GAN component
Hybrid quantum-classical setup makes advantage attribution unclear
The discriminator is classical, so the experiment is not a pure quantum-ML benchmark

notes: The GAN generator is explicitly implemented on a photonic chip, but the paper does not report a qubit count; the 8-bin demonstration is described in waveguide/path terms. Circuit depth is not numerically reported. No asymptotic speedup is claimed for the GAN itself; the paper frames it as a distribution-loading method.

The paper presents the GAN as a distribution-uploading module and reports convergence over 100 iterations with final L2 norm around -18 dB, but does not claim or demonstrate quantum advantage for this subtask.
